The best first experiment is a **learned recency residual added to SASRec**, evaluated through controlled perturbations. At 0% research progress, this offers a small, testable change aligned with the reported failure to prioritize current interests.

**Insights from the starting point.** (1) Existing margins measure training separation. They do not establish next-item generalization. (2) Qualitative feedback suggests that broad associations dilute recent, specific matches. Twenty users provide hypothesis-generating evidence, not population estimates. (3) The compatibility interface permits architecture changes. Probes must inspect the actual trained module and restore its previous evaluation mode.

**Insights from related work.** (1) Shuffling studies question whether benchmark gains require sequence order [1,2]. Order sensitivity alone therefore cannot demonstrate intent understanding. (2) Multi-window intent modeling motivates separating recent and historical evidence [3]. Its reported motivation does not establish that recency weighting will improve this benchmark. (3) Sampled ranking metrics can disagree with full-catalog metrics [4]. Selection must retain the pinned macro validation HR@10.

Three directions follow: measure temporal reliance; add a minimal recent-history pathway; and assess text-supported relevance while abstaining when evidence is missing.

| Framework component | Existing approach | Proposed extension | Remaining gap |
|---|---|---|---|
| Representation | SASRec sequence features | Recent embedding residual | Recent activity may reflect satisfied demand |
| Diagnosis | Training margins and geometry | Paired history perturbations | Reliance does not establish intent |
| Evidence | Titles/descriptions | Explicit text matches | Compatibility and user need remain uncertain |
| Selection | Pinned validation HR@10 | Same metric and routing | Full-catalog behavior may differ |

Three atomic ideas merit consideration. Scores are originality/potential/difficulty; higher difficulty means harder implementation.

| Idea | Scores | Positive assessment | Negative assessment |
|---|---|---|---|
| Paired recent-versus-old deletion audit [1,2] | 4/7/3 | Controlled, reusable diagnostic | Does not improve rankings directly |
| Learned recency residual [2,3] | 4/7/3 | Cheap, directly tests recency hypothesis | Familiar mechanism; may amplify redundant demand |
| TF–IDF title/description residual | 3/5/4 | Uses permitted content evidence | Surface overlap can reproduce reported errors |

**Selected algorithm.** At every training prefix, exponentially average its nonpadding item embeddings and add their candidate scores to SASRec scores. Learn one bounded residual coefficient per dataset; fix the decay horizon initially to avoid unnecessary search.

```python
r = weighted_mean(prefix_embeddings, exp(-interaction_age / 5))
r = layer_norm_without_affine(r)
score = sasrec_score + sigmoid(alpha) * dot(r, candidate_embedding)
loss = existing_training_loss(score, positives, negatives)
```

Initialize the coefficient near 0.05. Preserve baseline splits, seeds, loss, epochs, and optimizer for the first comparison. Save the coefficient and architecture settings, and update the predictor writer identically.

Extend diagnosis with fixed training-only pseudo-holdouts, matched recent/older deletions, last-item-preserving shuffles, paired target-rank changes, and top-10 overlap. Return unavailable measurements as null with counts and definitions. Select using four-category macro validation HR@10; bootstrap paired users within categories for uncertainty. These probes measure reliance, not observed intent, compatibility, or simulator traits.

idea.description: Add one learned, bounded recency residual coefficient to each dataset’s SASRec scorer. Combine ordinary SASRec logits with candidate logits from an exponentially weighted mean of embeddings in the observed prefix.
idea.motivation: Qualitative feedback identifies insufficient emphasis on specific recent interests. A small residual pathway tests this hypothesis while retaining the baseline sequence representation. Improvement remains an empirical question.
idea.implementation_notes: Use only observed prefix items, excluding padding; compute age in interaction steps with a fixed initial horizon of five. Apply parameter-free layer normalization to the pooled embedding and initialize sigmoid(alpha) near 0.05. Compute training residuals separately at every prefix to prevent future leakage. Preserve all four dataset routes, preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, SASREC_EPOCHS environment default 200, and DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR']. Store artifacts beneath the trial directory and include residual parameters and identical scoring logic in the predictor writer. Retain DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis). Use view.model as the trained module, preserve its prior training mode, and return metrics plus explicit metric_definitions. Implement perturbation comparisons on fixed training-only pseudo-holdouts and candidate sets; report missing evidence as null with sample counts. Do not access unavailable ratings, reviews, category metadata, or latent simulator traits. Compare against the baseline with the pinned host validation protocol; diagnostic pseudo-holdout HR must remain separately named. No performance improvement is claimed before execution.
idea.pseudocode:
For each dataset:
  initialize SASRec and alpha = log(0.05 / 0.95)
  for each baseline training batch:
    H = SASRec.log2feats(sequence)
    for each valid prefix ending at t:
      weights[j] = exp(-(t-j)/5), for nonpadding j <= t
      r[t] = parameter_free_layer_norm(weighted_mean(item_emb(sequence[j]), weights))
      score[t, candidate] = dot(H[t], item_emb(candidate)) + sigmoid(alpha) * dot(r[t], item_emb(candidate))
    optimize the unchanged baseline loss on positive and negative scores
  save model, alpha, decay horizon, and predictor architecture configuration
Compare the trained variant with baseline using the pinned four-category macro validation HR@10.
Run paired perturbation probes on training-only pseudo-holdouts; report reliance separately from benchmark selection.

originality.positive: Combines a minimal scoring change with explicit perturbation predictions tailored to the observed failure mode.
originality.negative: Recency pooling and residual scoring are established techniques; novelty lies mainly in the controlled experimental application.

future_potential.positive: Provides a reusable foundation for testing when recent behavior contributes information beyond SASRec.
future_potential.negative: Recent interactions cannot distinguish continuing demand from a need already satisfied, limiting the mechanism’s ability to address redundancy.

code_difficulty.positive: Adds one scalar per dataset and a prefix pooling operation without external data or additional encoders.
code_difficulty.negative: Correct prefix masking, consistent inference serialization, and paired perturbation bookkeeping require careful implementation.

related_work.title: [1] Does It Look Sequential? (2024)
contributions: The supplied research summary describes original-versus-shuffled history comparisons across 15 datasets, motivating controls for whether order contributes predictive value.
limitations: Shuffle sensitivity does not identify user intent or establish the benefit of the proposed residual.

related_work.title: [2] Disentangling User and Item Sequence Patterns (2025)
contributions: The supplied summary distinguishes random shuffling from shuffling constrained by item availability, highlighting catalog evolution as a possible explanation of sequential signal.
limitations: Availability controls require reliable availability information; first observed interaction timestamps are only proxies.

related_work.title: [3] MIMAR-SRec (2026)
contributions: The supplied summary describes intent modeling across temporal windows with robustness to interaction, temporal, and preference noise.
limitations: It motivates temporal separation but does not validate this simpler residual on the matched RecHarness task.

related_work.title: [4] Sampled recommendation metric analysis (IJCAI 2021)
contributions: Identifies systematic problems with sampled recommendation metrics, supporting strict separation of sampled-candidate selection and full-catalog diagnostics.
limitations: Does not remove the need to use the task’s pinned evaluation protocol or predict which proposed model will improve it.
